title: যুক্তব্যঞ্জন — Bangla Conjunct Consonants
summary: Learn how Bangla consonants join with হসন্ত (্), recognize 88 common conjuncts, and read each cluster through a familiar example word.
focus: conjunct formation, visual recognition, pronunciation, and whole-word reading

practice: Build a conjunct with হসন্ত: ক + ্ + ত = ক্ত. The first consonant loses its inherent vowel and joins the next consonant.

Read each conjunct through its example word instead of naming the component letters every time.
Compare easily confused shapes: ষ্ট in কষ্ট and ষ্ঠ in শ্রেষ্ঠ; ন্ট in প্যান্ট and ন্ড in ঠান্ডা.
Practice র clusters as visual chunks: র্ক, র্গ, র্চ, র্জ, র্ণ, র্ত, র্থ, র্দ, র্ধ, র্ন, র্প, র্ব, র্ম, র্শ, র্ষ, and র্স.
Practice s/sh clusters: শ্চ, শ্ন, শ্র, ষ্ক, ষ্ট, ষ্ঠ, ষ্ণ, ষ্প, ষ্ফ, স্ক, স্ট, স্ত, স্থ, স্ন, স্প, স্ফ, স্ম, and স্ব.

Compare true conjuncts with খণ্ড ত (ৎ): উৎপল, উৎফুল্ল, উৎস, and উৎসব use ৎ rather than the conjunct spellings ত্প, ত্ফ, ত্স, and ত্সব.
notes: Bangla conjunct consonants are called যুক্তব্যঞ্জন (juktobyanjon) or যুক্তাক্ষর (juktakkhor).
They form when two or more consonants combine, usually because the first consonant loses its inherent vowel through the হসন্ত sign ্.
Conjunct shapes and pronunciations are not always predictable. জ্ঞ in জ্ঞান and ক্ষ in ক্ষতি are best learned as complete visual chunks.
The examples for ন্স, র্ন, and ষ্প use ট্রান্স, কর্নার, and বাষ্প because these words visibly contain the stated conjuncts.
Start with the priority category, then learn the remaining families by their first consonant.
Part 2 adds common য-ফলা, র-ফলা, রেফ, doubled-consonant, and three-consonant clusters, along with rarer Sanskrit-derived and literary forms.

The starred supplied patterns র্দ্ধ, ল্ক্য, ষ্ট্য, ষ্ঠ্য, and স্ত্য were not added because their supplied examples do not reliably demonstrate standard modern Bangla conjunct spellings. The sequence র্পণ was also omitted as a separate conjunct because অর্পণ contains the conjunct র্প followed by ণ.
Two additional supplied rows were omitted after a spelling audit: মধ্যাহ্ন contains ধ্য plus হ্ন rather than ধ্ন, and অরণ্য contains ণ্য after a regular র rather than the conjunct র্ণ্য.

Part 3 includes only rows whose example visibly contains the exact conjunct. Derivative reading packets such as ঞ্চল, ঞ্জন, ঞ্জর, and প্টার were not treated as separate conjuncts because their final letters are not joined with another হসন্ত.

Some supplied Part 3 examples demonstrate a different spelling: সংখ্যা uses অনুস্বার plus খ্য rather than ঙ্খ্য; গ্রাহ্য does not contain গ্র্য; দগ্ধ does not contain দ্গ্ধ; and দৃশ্য does not contain র্শ্য.
Rows labeled only rare or uncommon without a verifiable example were not added as vocabulary items.
